name: codex mcp add
description: Register a Model Context Protocol server in ~/.codex/config.toml, either as a stdio launcher command after -- or as a streamable HTTP server with --url.

examples.explanation: Register a stdio server that Codex launches on demand.

examples.command: codex mcp add db --env PGURL=postgres://localhost/dev -- npx -y @org/pg-mcp
examples.explanation: Register a stdio server with an environment variable it needs at launch.

examples.command: codex mcp add example --url https://mcp.example.com --oauth-client-id my-client
examples.explanation: Register a streamable HTTP server with a pre-registered OAuth client.

when_to_use: Register a server without hand-editing config.toml.
when_not_to_use: Read the launcher command, URL, environment, and exposed tools before adding a server; MCP tools act outside the repository.

name: codex mcp list
description: List the MCP servers configured for Codex. Add --json for machine-readable output.

examples.explanation: Show the configured servers as a table.
Emit the configured servers as JSON for scripting.

name: codex mcp get
description: Print the stored configuration for a single MCP server. With --json, the raw config entry is printed.

examples.explanation: Inspect how one server is configured.
Print the raw config entry for that server.

name: codex mcp remove
description: Delete a stored MCP server definition from the Codex configuration.

examples.explanation: Remove a server Codex should no longer start.

name: codex mcp login
description: Start an OAuth login for a configured MCP server. OAuth actions work only with streamable HTTP servers, and only when the server supports OAuth.

examples.explanation: Run the OAuth flow for a streamable HTTP server.
Request specific OAuth scopes during login.
Force dynamic client registration for this login only.

when_not_to_use: Stdio servers do not use OAuth; there is nothing to log in to.

conditions: Streamable HTTP servers that support OAuth only.

name: codex mcp logout
description: Remove the stored OAuth credentials for a streamable HTTP MCP server.

examples.explanation: Drop stored OAuth credentials for one server.

conditions: Streamable HTTP servers that support OAuth only.

name: --url
display_name: Register a streamable HTTP MCP server
description: On codex mcp add, register a streamable HTTP server at the given URL instead of a stdio server. Mutually exclusive with the trailing stdio COMMAND.

examples.explanation: Add a streamable HTTP server.

name: --env
description: On codex mcp add, set environment variable assignments applied when launching a stdio MCP server. Repeatable.

examples.command: codex mcp add db --env PGURL=postgres://localhost/dev -- npx -y @org/pg-mcp
examples.explanation: Pass a connection string to a stdio server.

name: --bearer-token-env-var
display_name: Send a bearer token to an MCP server
description: On codex mcp add, name the environment variable whose value is sent as a bearer token when connecting to a streamable HTTP MCP server.

examples.command: codex mcp add example --url https://mcp.example.com --bearer-token-env-var EXAMPLE_TOKEN
examples.explanation: Authenticate with a static token held in the environment.

when_not_to_use: Prefer this over embedding a token in the configuration file, so the secret stays out of config.toml.

name: --oauth-client-id
description: On codex mcp add, supply the OAuth client identifier for a streamable HTTP MCP server whose authorization server requires a pre-registered client. Requires --url.

examples.command: codex mcp add example --url https://mcp.example.com --oauth-client-id my-client
examples.explanation: Add a server that needs a pre-registered OAuth client.

name: --oauth-resource
display_name: Set the MCP OAuth resource parameter
description: On codex mcp add, include an OAuth resource parameter during login for a streamable HTTP MCP server. Requires --url.

examples.command: codex mcp add example --url https://mcp.example.com --oauth-resource https://api.example.com
examples.explanation: Scope the OAuth login to one protected resource.

name: --scopes
description: On codex mcp login, request a comma-separated list of OAuth scopes for the login.

examples.explanation: Ask for two scopes during the OAuth flow.

name: --oauth-client-registration
description: On codex mcp login, choose the OAuth client-registration strategy for this login only: auto, cimd, or dcr. The default is auto, and the choice is not stored in configuration.

examples.explanation: Use client ID metadata documents for one login.
Use dynamic client registration for one login.

name: codex plugin add
description: Install a plugin from a configured marketplace snapshot. Pass PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE, or pass PLUGIN with --marketplace.

examples.explanation: Install a plugin from a named marketplace.
Name the marketplace separately when the selector omits it.
Print pluginId, name, marketplaceName, version, installedPath, and authPolicy for automation.

when_not_to_use: A plugin runs with your Codex session's reach; install only from marketplaces you trust.

name: codex plugin list
description: List installed plugins. With --json the output has installed and available arrays; --available adds uninstalled marketplace plugins and requires --json.

examples.explanation: Show the installed plugins.
Restrict the listing to one configured marketplace.
Include uninstalled marketplace plugins in machine-readable output.

name: codex plugin remove
description: Remove an installed plugin from local config and cache. Pass PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE, or pass PLUGIN with --marketplace.

examples.explanation: Uninstall a plugin.
Name the marketplace separately when the selector omits it.

name: codex plugin marketplace add
description: Add a marketplace source Codex can browse and install from: GitHub shorthand, an HTTP or HTTPS Git URL, an SSH Git URL, or a local marketplace root directory.

examples.explanation: Add a local marketplace root.

examples.command: codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo --ref main
examples.explanation: Add a Git marketplace pinned to a ref.

examples.command: codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/owner/repo --sparse plugins/foo
examples.explanation: Sparse-check out one path from a Git marketplace.

when_not_to_use: Adding a marketplace is what makes its plugins installable; add only sources you trust.

name: codex plugin marketplace list
description: Show the plugin marketplaces Codex is currently considering and the root path for each, including implicitly discovered default marketplaces and configured snapshots.

examples.explanation: See which marketplaces are in scope and where they resolve.
Emit a marketplaces array for scripting.

name: codex plugin marketplace upgrade
description: Refresh configured Git marketplace snapshots. Name one marketplace, or omit the name to upgrade every configured Git marketplace.

examples.explanation: Refresh every configured Git marketplace.
Refresh one marketplace by name.

conditions: Git-backed marketplaces only; local marketplace roots are read in place.

name: codex plugin marketplace remove
description: Remove a configured plugin marketplace source by name.

examples.explanation: Stop considering one marketplace source.

name: --marketplace
display_name: Name the marketplace for a plugin command
description: On codex plugin add, list, and remove, name the configured marketplace to use when the plugin selector omits @MARKETPLACE. Short form: -m.

examples.explanation: Install a plugin from a specific marketplace.
List only the plugins from one marketplace.

name: --available
description: On codex plugin list, include uninstalled marketplace plugins in the output. Requires --json.

examples.explanation: See installed and installable plugins together.

name: --ref
description: On codex plugin marketplace add, fetch a specific Git ref for a Git-backed marketplace source.

examples.command: codex plugin marketplace add owner/repo --ref main
examples.explanation: Track a named branch instead of the default ref.

name: --sparse
description: On codex plugin marketplace add, use a sparse checkout of the given path for a Git-backed marketplace. Repeatable.

examples.command: codex plugin marketplace add https://github.com/owner/repo --sparse plugins/foo
examples.explanation: Fetch only one plugin directory from a large repository.

name: --json
description: Emit machine-readable JSON instead of formatted text. Documented on codex mcp get and list, codex plugin add, list, and remove, every codex plugin marketplace subcommand, codex cloud list, and every codex remote-control subcommand.

examples.explanation: Read installed and available plugin arrays from a script.
Read pairingCode, manualPairingCode, environmentId, and expiresAt as JSON.

conditions: Not accepted by every subcommand; check the subcommand's own documentation.

name: codex features list
description: Show known feature flags, their maturity stage, and their effective state.

examples.explanation: See which optional features are on before changing them.

name: codex features enable
description: Persistently enable a feature flag in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml.

examples.explanation: Turn a feature on for every later session.

when_to_use: Keep a feature on across sessions, rather than passing --enable each run.

name: codex features disable
description: Persistently disable a feature flag in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml.

examples.explanation: Turn a feature off for every later session.

name: codex remote-control start
description: Start the local app-server daemon with remote control enabled. Running codex remote-control without a subcommand starts remote control in the foreground instead.

examples.explanation: Start the managed daemon in the background.

when_not_to_use: This is not a replacement for codex app-server --listen when you are building a local protocol client.

name: codex remote-control stop
description: Stop the local app-server daemon started with remote control enabled.

examples.explanation: Shut the managed daemon down.

name: codex remote-control pair
description: Create and print a short-lived manual pairing code once the daemon is running. With --json the response includes pairingCode, manualPairingCode, environmentId, and expiresAt.

examples.explanation: Print a pairing code to enter on another device.
Read the pairing code and its expiry from a script.

name: codex cloud exec
description: Submit a task to Codex cloud without launching the TUI. --env is required; if the prompt is omitted, Codex asks for it interactively. Codex exits non-zero when submission fails.

examples.command: codex cloud exec --env env_123 "Fix the failing unit tests"
examples.explanation: Submit one cloud task and return.

examples.command: codex cloud exec --env env_123 --attempts 4 "Fix the failing unit tests"
examples.explanation: Ask for four independent attempts and pick the best.

when_to_use: Queue work from a script or CI without holding a terminal open.

conditions: Requires Codex cloud access and the same credentials as the main CLI.

name: codex cloud list
description: List recent cloud chats with optional environment filtering and pagination. Plain-text output prints a task URL followed by status details; --json returns a tasks array plus an optional cursor.

examples.explanation: See recent cloud tasks and their status.
Show the five most recent tasks in one environment.
Continue a paginated listing from a previous cursor.

conditions: Requires Codex cloud access and the same credentials as the main CLI.

name: --attempts
description: On codex cloud exec, set the number of assistant attempts (best-of-N) Codex cloud should run, from 1 to 4.

examples.command: codex cloud exec --env env_123 --attempts 4 "Fix the failing unit tests"
examples.explanation: Run four attempts on a task worth extra compute.

name: --limit
description: On codex cloud list, set the maximum number of tasks to return, from 1 to 20.

examples.explanation: Show only the five most recent tasks.

name: --cursor
description: On codex cloud list, continue a listing from the pagination cursor returned by a previous request.

examples.explanation: Fetch the next page of tasks.

name: codex login status
display_name: Show the active Codex auth mode
description: Print the active authentication mode and exit with 0 when credentials are present, which makes it usable as a guard in automation scripts.

examples.explanation: Check whether this machine is logged in.
Fall back to an API key login when no credentials are present.

name: --device-auth
display_name: Log in with a device code
description: On codex login, use the OAuth device code flow instead of launching a browser window.

examples.explanation: Log in from a machine with no browser, such as an SSH session.

name: --with-access-token
display_name: Log in with a piped access token
description: On codex login, read an access token from stdin rather than prompting.

examples.explanation: Authenticate a CI runner from an environment secret.

when_not_to_use: Pipe the token from a secret store or environment variable so it never reaches shell history.

name: --with-api-key
display_name: Log in with a piped API key
description: On codex login, read an API key from stdin rather than prompting.

examples.explanation: Authenticate with an API key held in the environment.

when_not_to_use: Pipe the key from a secret store or environment variable so it never reaches shell history.
